data.title: Warner Bros. studio execs to leave after Paramount merger -- Variety
data.description:
Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy will reportedly step down as co-heads of Warner Bros. Pictures (WBD) once the studio merges with Paramount Skydance (PSKY) this month.

According to sources cited by Variety, De Luca and Abdy, the team behind "Sinners," "One Battle After Another," "Weapons," and the upcoming “Dune: Part 3,” will not be a part of a merged Paramount/Warner Bros. executive team. Instead, Paramount Pictures co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein will run the merged Paramount Warner Bros. Motion Picture unit.

The decision to leave De Luca and Abdy out of the new Skydance comes shortly after the pair extended their Warner Bros. contracts through 2030.

The merger of Paramount Skydance (PSKY) and Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) will be completed October 6, at which time the new company will be renamed Skydance. Former Mattel (MAT) CEO Ynon Kreiz will lead the new company along with current CEO David Ellison.

data.title: CoreWeave in focus as UBS sees AI infrastructure market staying hot
data.description:
CoreWeave (CRWV) was in focus on Friday as UBS said it sees the artificial intelligence infrastructure market staying hot.

“There is widespread acknowledgement that the per-hour price of hosted Nvidia GPUs is rising, we are in an inflationary environment, and that revs/GW figures are moving higher, now a key pillar of the hyperscaler and neo-cloud bull case (even though it will take time to work through the P&Ls),” UBS analyst Karl Keirstead wrote in a note to clients. “CoreWeave disclosed this week that it raised per-hour GPU pricing across all SKUs by 25% in July 2026 and that since then (so just in the last 2-3 months) it has raised them by another 10%. 2. Could the new bottleneck of local community and, hence, state/local government pushback throttle the pace of AI data center adds? The risk is real, but the consensus from our checks was that the AI industry will manage through this hurdle as it has with others, and our checks were even more sanguine about this risk than we expected.”

Delving deeper, Keirstead said the availability and the cost of capital could hurt the pace of the AI buildout. Recent checks have concluded some projects will wind up fading, but the “better-positioned players” will not have an issue, Keirstead added, including CoreWeave.

data.title: Alerus, Horizon Bancorp, IBCP upgraded at Piper, two stocks downgraded
data.description:
After a selloff in small-cap Midwest bank stocks, Piper Sandler upgraded Alerus Financial (ALRS), Horizon Bancorp (HBNC), and Independent Bank (IBCP) to Overweight from Neutral and lowered First Busey (BUSE) and Equity Bancshares (EQBK) to Neutral from Overweight.

Alerus stock rose 2.1%, Horizon Bancorp gained 2.5%, and Independent Bank (IBCP) increased 1.6% in midday trading Friday. The downgrades saw milder stock action. First Busey (BUSE) stock rose 0.9%, and Equity Bancshares (EQBK) gained 0.4%.

In determining the ratings changes, analyst Nathan Race focused on factors expected to drive future growth, such as disciplined and high-quality mid-single-digit organic growth on both sides of the balance sheet, defensible-to-expanding net interest margins, preprovision net revenue upside drivers, and relatively benign credit.

For Horizon (HBNC), Piper expects the bank's peer profitability guidance and mid-single-digit organic balance sheet growth to narrow the shares' ~2x forward P/E discount vs. its peers.

Race said drivers for Alerus (ALRS) include "solid prospects for NIM and B/S growth outperformance amid seemingly conservative guidance on both fronts."

Meanwhile, Independent Bank's (IBCP) strong profitability outlook and solid EPS growth outlook for 2027, combined with its recently closed HBCP acquisition, warrant better valuation than its current ~1x discount to peers on forward earnings.

First Busey (BUSE) was downgraded following recent outperformance and uncertain timing regarding its prospects to consistently generate at least low- to mid-single-digit organic growth, Piper's Race said.

He attributed the Equity Bancshares (EQBK) to "uncertain timing around EQBK’s prospects to garner more of a peer-like valuation on forward earnings."

Piper's ratings align with the SA Quant system's ratings for Alerus (ALRS), Independent Bank (IBCP), and Equity Bancshares (EQBK). However, they disagree with the the SA Quant rating of Hold for Horizon (HBNC) and Strong Buy for First Busey (BUSE).

data.title: Wall Street rallied and yields moved back higher after the latest payrolls data
data.description:
U.S. equities climbed Friday after the September nonfarm payrolls report came in cooler than economists expected.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last +0.3%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was +0.7%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last +1.3%. 

From a sector-by-sector basis, eight of the 11 segments moved up in the green and were led by info tech. At the other end of the spectrum, healthcare struggled the most.

U.S. employers added just 29K jobs in September, well short of the 85K consensus figure and a sharp slowdown from August’s downwardly revised gain of 133K (from 162K), the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Friday. 

“Not only were the 29K jobs created in Sept. below expectations, but as I predicted last month, July and Aug. were revised down by 31K and 29K respectively. My guess is that all three months will ultimately be revised even lower. We have a weak labor market with strong inflation,” Peter Schiff of Europac stated. 

Treasury yields were lower early on but have since pushed back up. The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) moved up 3 basis points to 4.82%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) moved higher by 2 basis points to 5.26%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) pushed up 1 basis point to 5.62%. 

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of ON Semiconductor (ON) advanced +5.3%, while shares of Seagate Technology (STX) fell -12.7%.

data.title: Pfizer says phase 3 data buoys Litfulo as a vitiligo treatment
data.description:
• Pfizer (PFE) said that full results from two phase 3 studies of its alopecia drug Litfulo (ritlecitinib) found that the treatment led to significant improvements in facial and total body repigmentation in patients with vitiligo after a year compared to placebo.
  • The studies, TRANQUILLO 2 and TRANQUILLO, tested Litfulo at dosages of, respectively, 100 mg and 50 mg daily.
  • In TRANQUILLO 2 and TRANQUILLO, 21.86% and 12.47%, respectively, of patients on Litfulo achieved F-VASI75 (≥75% improvement in Facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index) vs. 2.40% and 2.48% on placebo.
  • Data for the other co-primary endpoint, achieving T-VASI50 (≥50% improvement in Total Vitiligo Area Scoring Index), was, respectively, 13.02% and 8.98% compared to  2.40% and 1.98% for placebo.
  • Pfizer also said that  improvements from baseline in F-VASI and T-VASI were seen as early as week 24 and increased from there.
  • The drugmaker said it plans to submit the new data to drug regulators for review. 
  • Pfizer released topline data on Litfulo for vitiligo in late July.

data.title: Qiagen gains on report talks with strategic buyer have advanced
data.description:
Qiagen (QGEN) advanced 7.3% on a report that discussions between the company and a US-listed molecular testing company are speculated to have advanced.

At least one possible buyer is in advanced talks to buy Qiagen (QGEN) for a "realistic premium," according to traders, who cited a Betaville "uncooked" alert that was circulating on Friday.

The latest update comes after Manager Magazin reported that private equity firms TPG Inc. (TPG) and Bain Capital were interested in acquiring the diagnostics firm. KKR & Co. (KKR), EQT, and Advent are also looking at Qiagen.  CTFN reported in August that two parties started formal due diligence on Qiagen (QGEN) as part of the molecular diagnostics provider's strategic review.

Bloomberg first reported in July that the European molecular testing company was seeing early takeover interest from EQT AB and Advent.

Qiagen (QGEN) said in March the company was working with Moelis & Co. and Goldman Sachs to review its strategic alternatives.

In August 2020, Thermo Fisher (TMO) walked away from a €43.00 per share offer for diagnostic test maker Qiagen (QGEN). Thermo Fisher first announced a €39/share offer for QGEN in March 2020, and then upped its bid after institutional investors rebelled over the price.

data.title: Northrop Grumman downgraded at RBC on lower growth outlook; Arxis upgraded
data.description:
Northrop Grumman (NOC) down 1.2% in Friday's trading as RBC Capital downgraded the defense company to Sector Perform from Outperform with a $525 price target, lowered from $640, saying that while Northrop has demonstrated better execution than peers, comparable growth will not justify a valuation premium.

RBC analyst Ken Herbert said investors did not place a high probability on Northrop's (NOC) chances on the F/A-XX, which was recently awarded to Boeing, but the ability to see upside revenue surprises for Northrop now rests with the B-21, the space portfolio, and potentially the solid rocket motor portfolio, all of which likely would entail some level of incremental investment that would impact market sentiment.

Herbert also said Northrop (NOC) is less exposed to international sales, slower budget growth post-FY 2027 limits the company's potential upside, and limited capital allocation options restrictpotential catalysts.

Moreover, Northrop (NOC) looks unlikely to outgrow its defense peers, and broader investor concerns about growth in defense spending should remain a headwind to sentiment across the sector, the analyst said.

Arxis (ARXS) gained 2.8% on Friday as Herbert upgraded shares to Outperform from Sector Perform with a $60 PT, raised from $50, saying the company is "one of the best-positioned in our coverage to benefit from pricing strength across its end markets," and consensus 2027-28 estimates "do not fully reflect the M&A and execution upside."

data.title: Midday Need to Know: Payrolls data, factory orders, and more
data.description:
U.S. stocks pushed higher Friday after September nonfarm payrolls landed softer than Wall Street had penciled in.

The Dow (DJI) was last up +0.3%, the S&P 500 (SP500) gained +0.6%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) led with a +1.2% advance.

Now, here are three news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:

The latest payrolls report came in softer than expected: U.S. employers added just 29K jobs in September, well short of the 85K consensus figure and a sharp slowdown from August’s downwardly revised gain of 133K (from 162K), the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Friday. At the same time, the unemployment rate picked up to 4.2% from 4.1% in the prior month and exceeded the 4.1% consensus.

Factory orders moved higher: U.S. factory orders rose 0.1% to $663.5B in August, its second straight increase. The indicator topped the 0.0% consensus and decelerated from +0.8% in July (revised from +0.9%), according to data released by the U.S. Census Bureau.

Amazon moved higher on chip positioning: Amazon (AMZN) is seeking to offload about $8B of advanced Nvidia (NVDA) chips to external investors through a new special-purpose vehicle, the Financial Times reported on Friday. The decision aims to improve the tech group's balance sheet health as AI spending soars.
